title: Freight bid-eval LLM pilot scoping and SOW draft
content:
Executive summary:

This doc is a working SOW + scoping note for a proposed 8-week Freight Bid Evaluation pilot with a mid-sized TMS provider (prospect: FreightLogic). Goal: demonstrate how Redwood Inference can (a) automatically evaluate and score incoming carrier bids against historical outcomes and business rules, and (b) surface structured rationale to operations teams to speed load acceptance decisions and reduce cost-per-load.

High-level pilot goals:
- Build a repeatable pipeline to ingest tender/capacity bid data + historical shipments from FreightLogic's Postgres + S3 archive.
- Produce per-bid latent embeddings and a ranking score for each carrier bid using a lightweight retriever + re-ranker architecture.
- Expose a demo UI / API for operations to query rank, explanations, and sensitivity (what-if price or ETA changes).
- Run a 2-week shadow test on a subset (5–10% of tenders) and measure decision alignment, time saved, and cost delta.

Scope of work (8 weeks, broken down):
Week 0: Kickoff & data discovery (1 week)
- Onsite/remote kickoff workshop (2 hours): ops stakeholders, data engineer, SRE, product owner.
- Deliverables: data inventory, access plan, security checklist, sample export of 500 tenders.

Week 1–2: Data pipeline + feature extraction (2 weeks)
- Connector build: bulk export from Postgres (tenders, lanes, historical booked rates), S3 object listing for PODs/attachments.
- ETL: normalize carrier codes, lane canonicalization, date parsing, currency normalization.
- Feature engineering: transit-time distributions, on-time rates, claim history counts, tender acceptance latencies.
- Deliverable: cleaned dataset and README of transformations.

Week 3–4: Modeling & retrieval layer (2 weeks)
- Embedding model: seed with a pre-trained shipping-domain embedding (e.g., fine-tune on FreightLogic historical text fields).
- Retriever index (FAISS or Redwood-managed index): nearest neighbors for comparable historical shipments.
- Re-ranker: small cross-encoder to produce final score and natural-language rationale.
- Deliverable: model artifact, index snapshot, local eval metrics (NDCG@10, recall).

Week 5: Integration + API + demo UI (1 week)
- Expose inference endpoints via Redwood Hosted API (or Dedicated trial).
- Simple demo UI for ops: query by tender id, view top-5 comparable past loads, score breakdown (price impact, transit risk, capacity reliability).
- Deliverable: demo URL, API docs, short training video.

Week 6–7: Shadow run + metrics (2 weeks)
- Run side-by-side on live tenders for 2 weeks.
- Metrics: percent of ops decisions aligned, average time-to-decision, average price delta if model suggested alternate.
- Deliverable: shadow-run report + recommended threshold for pilot production.

Week 8: Wrap & production plan (1 week)
- Final report, risk register, recommended architecture for production (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), cost estimates and expected ROI.
- Handoff package: infra config, runbook, evaluation prompts and test suites.

Assumptions & constraints:
- Access: FreightLogic provides read-only credentials to a staging Postgres and S3; no PHI.
- Data volume: 2 years of history (approx 700k shipments). If larger, index cost may increase.
- SLA: Pilot uses Redwood Hosted endpoints with best-effort latency; production SLOs to be negotiated.

Deployment options discussed:
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood API, low setup time, logs stored in Redwood console. Good for rapid demo and shadowing.
- Dedicated (recommended for pilot scale beyond shadow): reserved pool, predictable throughput for batch scoring during peak tender windows.
- Private/VPC: required only if FreightLogic insists on on-premise-only data residency. Longer lead time.

Pricing (draft estimates) — pilot total fixed fee + variable usage:
- Professional Services (8 weeks): $78,000 (SWE + ML eng + solutions lead + PM + 2x workshops).
- Infra & inference estimate (pilot): $6,500 (Redwood Hosted inference + index storage + S3 egress estimates).
- Optional: Dedicated trial (4-weeks reserved) add $28,000 if customer wants capacity guarantees during shadow run.
- Total pilot cost (hosted path): $84,500.

Pricing notes: rough order of magnitude only. Final price will vary if data cleaning effort >20 engineer-hours or security review requires private deployment. Add travel expenses if on-site workshop requested.

Success criteria (proposal):
- Model produces ranking that matches ops' chosen carrier in >= 70% of shadowed tenders.
- Median time-to-decision for ops reduces by >= 30%.
- Demonstrable cost-per-load improvement (or at minimum identify 3 high-value load types for optimization).

Workshop and playbook outline (kickoff):
- 10-min product intro + demo of Redwood inference capabilities.
- 30-min ops walkthrough: what decisions look like today (fields, heuristics).
- 30-min data deep-dive with data engineer: schemas, sample payloads.
- 20-min technical Q&A and risk discussion (PII, retention, audit).
- End with 10 min: agree on next steps and access checklist.

Risks & open questions (notes to self / unresolved):
- Q: Will FreightLogic accept storing model indices off-prem? If not, private deployment estimate needed.
- Q: Currency conversion logic — do we normalize to USD or keep lane-currency? Need confirmation.
- Data quality risk: inconsistent carrier IDs across older records; may need mapping table from ops.
- Integration: can we get webhook on tender publish? If yes, we can test near-real-time scoring during shadow.

Action items (short term):
- [ ] Send SOW + pilot quote to FreightLogic procurement (Owner: Marco).
- [ ] Schedule kickoff for week of Oct 7 (Owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Prep sample data template and Parquet export instructions (Owner: DataEng).

Appendix — quick technical choices rationale:
- Retriever + re-ranker chosen because many successful logistics workloads rely on retrieving comparable historic cases rather than pure parametric prediction. Makes explanations easier for ops.
- Embeddings: start with a small 384-d model to keep index size and recall tradeoffs manageable; can upgrade to 1536-d for better semantic fidelity if needed.
- Quantization: recommend int8 quantized models for Dedicated if customer wants lower cost tokens.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated lane queries to reduce token cost during bulk scoring.

Notes: this is a working draft — expect edits after kickoff. Keep SOW lean; avoid >10% bucketed contingencies in initial pricing.

---
Workshop scribbles (raw / unedited):
- ops: "we want 'why this carrier' — not just a number" -> include 3 bullet rationale lines + top-3 features driving score.
- data: missing POD link field for ~12% of rows; fallback to notes text.
- prod suggestion: expose a simple explain endpoint returning top-3 historical comparators + delta simulation for +/- $50 price change.
- TODO: collect list of non-negotiable business rules (preferred lanes, contracted carriers) to hard-filter model outputs.

End of doc.
